feedback.text: Adding the legs does not find the hypotenuse.

Subtracting the legs does not use the Pythagorean Theorem.

Question ID: GEO_U04_L05_Q11

MLA Standard: Readiness Support Only

A right triangle has hypotenuse 5 and one leg 3. What is the other leg?

feedback.text: Subtracting side lengths ignores the squared relationship.
Use b? = 5? - 3?; the missing leg is 4.
Adding the known lengths does not find a missing leg.

answer.text: sqrt(34)

feedback.text: Adding squares would be used if both known sides were legs, but 5 is the hypotenuse.
